results.text: Double Peaking Phenomena in Pharmacokinetic Disposition Revisited. Multiple peaking in pharmacokinetics refers to the occurrence of two or more peaks of drug plasma concentrations following a single dose administration. It complicates interpretation of pharmacokinetics parameters and influences clinical decision-making regarding drug efficacy and bioequivalence. Pharmacokinetics and multi-peak phenomenon analysis of novel anti-Parkinson's drug FLZ after multi-dose in cynomolgus monkeys. The novel anti-Parkinson disease drug, FLZ, had a complicated drug absorption and metabolise process reported in single-dose studies. A multi-peak absorption peak phenomenon was found.This study focused on the multi-dose pharmacokinetics (PK) characteristics of FLZ, T1, and T2 in cynomolgus monkeys and raised discussion on its multi-peak absorption situation.
